The Future: Going To – Negative Statements
You use going to to talk about future plans or intentions that have been planned or prepared before.

To create negative statements using going to you need to use the following grammar structure:

Subject + verb to be + not + going to + main verb in its base form + complement

Example:

She is not going to fail the test.

I’mnot going to work tonight at the warehouse.

They are not going to store all their products in their warehouses.

Data Warehouse Architecture
There are some important properties that build data warehouse architecture.

We can define data warehouse as the gathering of information that helps managers, directors and analysts to make certain decision in the management of a warehouse. Let’s take a look at the five essential properties of data warehouse architecture.

Separation: It is the property which determines that analytical and transactional processing must remain apart.

Scalability: It is the property which states that hardware and software architectures must be easy to upgrade or improve. This is due to the fact that the data volume and the number of user’s requirements are increasing progressively.

Extensibility: It is the property which determines that the architecture of a warehouse must be able to include or work with the technologies and applications without having to restructure the system.

Security: This property states that monitoring access is vital as there is strategic data stored in data warehouses.

Administerability: It is the property which defines that data warehouse management shouldn’t be too complicated.

images.text: Today we are going to cover two important topics related to data warehouse: Tools and utilities and architecture. We are not going to go over other aspects of data warehouse during this session as I expect to provide detailed information on the two topics I just mentioned.

I'm starting with tools and utilities. We are going to use five different tools and utilities when working with data warehouse. The first one is data extraction, which refers to the gathering of data from various sources. We are not going to limit ourselves to using only homogeneous sources as a larger variety of these will make our analysis more complete. The second one is data cleaning that we will use when finding and correcting mistakes in data. Thirdly, we have data transformation which refers to the process of converting data from a legacy format to a warehouse one. Then, we are using data loading when sorting, consolidating, summarizing and building indices and partitions in order to make data more comprehensible and practical to use. Finally, we are going to work with refreshing which refers to the process of updating data sources to warehouses.

Now, for our second topic, data warehouse architecture, we are going to go over five different properties. The first one is separation, which we are going to consider when handling data since analytical and transactional processing must remain apart. The second one, scalability, refers to the easy upgrade of hardware and software architectures. This is due to the fact that our business is not going to be at a standstill, but is expected to have a progressive increase in the data volume and the number of user’s requirements. As a third property, we will have extensibility which determines that we are not going to have to restructure the whole system when the architecture includes new technologies and applications. Fourthly, security refers to the importance of the monitoring accesses as there is strategic data stored in data warehouses and knowing who accesses this information will ensure that data remains safe. Finally, we are going to consider administerability as data warehouse management mustn’t be too complex or hard to handle.

Alright, I’m passing the list of articles you’ll have to read for next session. See you on Monday and the class is dismissed.
